profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's Silicon Valley (Santa Clara/San Jose area) data center campus, one of the company's largest US clusters. Two facilities in this group carry independent historic significance: 360 Spear Street and 365 Main Street in San Francisco are separate, well known carrier hotel buildings; 365 Main Street was the site of a widely covered July 2007 power outage that took down major web services including Craigslist and other sites hosted there, later becoming a Digital Realty/Digital Realty-heritage asset. SJC10 is documented at 1100 Space Park Drive per Digital Realty's own site.

reading.body:
This facility's critical IT power capacity is not published by Digital Realty on the operator's spec page. Without that figure, no estimate can be made of the number of racks or accelerators this campus can house. The campus is ranked 12th among California facilities with published megawatt capacity, but it does not appear in the 11 facilities whose operators have disclosed watts in this state.

Digital Realty operates SJC30 as part of a Silicon Valley cluster in Santa Clara County that includes other named facilities such as SJC10 at 1100 Space Park Drive. The company also holds significant legacy assets in the region stemming from historic carrier hotels in San Francisco, including 365 Main Street, which was the site of a 2007 power outage that disrupted major web services. The firm's long tenure in the Bay Area data center market suggests established grid relationships and customer bases, but specific certifications or compliance credentials for this facility are not published.

Of 103 data center facilities mapped in California, only 11 operators have published megawatt figures, totaling 365 MW of disclosed capacity. SJC30's omission from that 11 means its power footprint, whether large or small, is not visible in the public record. Any assessment of its role in AI infrastructure scaling cannot proceed without disclosure of its IT load.
